input: Choose a charity to volunteer with quarterly

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which causes or types of charities the user cares about narrows the field from thousands of options to a relevant shortlist.
Whether the user is volunteering solo, with family, friends, or a work group changes which charities are suitable and what activities make sense.
Whether the volunteering must be local/in-person or can be remote affects which organizations are even accessible to the user.
How many hours per quarter the user can commit directly shapes which roles and charities are realistic — some require multi-day commitments, others just a few hours.
The type of activity the user enjoys (hands-on physical work, skilled professional help, mentoring, admin, etc.) determines which volunteering roles will feel rewarding vs. draining.
Understanding what the user most wants to get out of volunteering (community connection, skill-building, impact in a specific area, etc.) defines what a good choice actually looks like.
Knowing whether the user wants a shortlist to research independently or a single recommended charity to commit to right away determines the output format of the plan.

gold.taskTitle: Choose a charity to volunteer with quarterly
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to select a charity organization to volunteer with on a quarterly basis.

questions.title: Which cause areas matter most to you?
questions.description: Identify the user's priority causes — e.g., food insecurity, animal welfare, education, environment, homelessness — to filter the charity landscape to relevant options.

questions.title: Will you be volunteering alone or with others?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a solo commitment or involves family members, friends, or a workplace group, as this affects activity type and charity fit.

questions.title: Does it need to be local, or is remote volunteering okay?
questions.description: Establish whether in-person presence at a physical location is required or if virtual/remote volunteering is acceptable.

questions.title: How many hours per quarter can you realistically commit?
questions.description: Pin down the time budget — a few hours in a single day, a full weekend, or spread across multiple sessions — to match charities whose volunteer requirements fit.

questions.title: What kind of volunteer activity do you most enjoy?
questions.description: Understand the user's preferred activity style — hands-on physical tasks, skilled or professional contributions, mentoring, fundraising, admin — to match role types.

questions.title: What do you most want to get out of volunteering?
questions.description: Clarify the user's primary personal goal — building community, gaining new skills, making direct impact, fulfilling a personal value — to define what a successful choice looks like.

questions.title: Do you want one final pick or a shortlist to compare?
questions.description: Determine whether the output should be a single charity recommendation to commit to immediately or a curated shortlist the user can evaluate and choose from.
